findings.note: The containment claim behind sandbox evidence is a comment, not a mechanism, and it is duplicated in three files. internal/fsm/judge/judge.go:201-203 says WithCodexWorkDir 'returns j with its codex judge confined to dir', that it is 'the containment half of sandbox evidence', and that handing the CLI a materialized tree 'is what makes "the evidence" an enumerable set'; judge.go:186-187 says codexWorkDir 'narrows a codex judge to a materialized evidence tree'. The whole implementation is judge.go:211 (clone.codexWorkDir = dir) -> judge.go:533 (workDir on codexJudge) -> internal/fsm/cli/deps.go:109 (cmd.Dir = dir). A process's working directory is the resolution root for relative paths; it is not a read boundary - the child can still open any absolute path, and `..` walks out of the tree in one hop. The flag that is a boundary, `--sandbox read-only` at internal/fsm/judge/codex.go:59, restricts writes and network, not the read set, and its own comment says so ('a judge reads; it must never edit the tree it is judging'). So the second-opinion judge can read metareview's own repository, the real working tree the sandbox was copied from, and anything else on the box, and the Escalation's recorded TreeHash/BaseSHA/HeadSHA (internal/fsm/cli/escalation.go:50-57) describe the tree that was *offered*, not the evidence the verdict rests on. deps.go:107-108 states the falsehood outright: 'A caller that has materialized an evidence tree passes it here so the CLI cannot read past it.' This is the class the branch's own new RubricAddendum instructs judges to treat as real (internal/fsm/judge/prompts.go, 'a comment, doc line, test name or specification row that asserts a property the code does not have is a real finding, even when the code behaves correctly, because the next reader will rely on it'), and the reliance is concrete: the next reader sees 'containment' and does not add the boundary. Mutation confirms the asymmetry - deleting the assignment at judge.go:211 or the wiring at judge.go:533 reddens four tests, so the *plumbing* is pinned, while no test anywhere asserts that a read outside the tree fails, because nothing makes it fail. Fix: either state the real property (it sets the CLI's working directory so relative paths resolve inside the evidence tree, and is not a read boundary) in all three places, or make it true - run codex under a sandbox profile rooted at the tree, and only then call the recorded hashes an audit record.

Add a usage line, the Commands entry, and a baseline grep alongside the existing ones.

findings.note: The spec row introducing the two confirmed-side verdicts describes one of its own cases wrongly. docs/specs/2026-08-27-metareview-0.9.0-fsm-judge-kinds.md:261-263 defines 'checked_but_unverified: a judge WAS asked and returned no usable answer' and closes by insisting the two verdicts are distinct because '"no one could look" is not "a judge looked and was unsure"'. At internal/fsm/kind/kind.go:583-587 the escalation could not be *built* (resolve returned an error from sandbox materialization or judge construction): no second judge was asked at all, and the first arm did return a usable answer - it decided not-real. Both halves of the sentence are false on that path, and it is exactly the '"no one could look"' case the row says this verdict is not. The parenthetical 'or a failed escalation' names the case but contradicts the clause it qualifies, so a human triaging the two verdicts is told the opposite of what the code does. Either widen the definition ('a judge was asked and gave no usable answer, or a second opinion that was required could not be obtained') or split the failed-escalation path off.
